findings.label: control-flow
findings.failure_mode: a Brief-probes block that succeeds but writes an incidental diagnostic to stderr sets BRIEF_DEGRADED=1 and reports brief.txt as possibly incomplete even though nothing actually failed
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:376 — eval "$PROBES" ... 2>"$OUT/brief-probes-stderr" captures every byte of stderr from the block, not just failures
build-artifacts.sh:377 — if [ -s "$OUT/brief-probes-stderr" ]; then treats any non-empty stderr as an error
build-artifacts.sh:378-379 — BRIEF_DEGRADED=1 and a 'may be missing whatever it would have added' note are emitted for a fully successful run that merely logged to stderr

findings.label: contract
findings.failure_mode: a pack that fails validate-pack.sh for a reason unrelated to Wiring files (e.g. a malformed Label-probes row) gets PACK_INVALID=1/STALE=1, which this diff documents as degrading identically to a stale pack across wiring.txt/probes-*.txt, but wiring.txt's extraction only checks PACK_PRESENT and still writes the invalid pack's Wiring files block verbatim
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md:28 — "PACK_STALE=1 empties wiring.txt/probes-*.txt" is the documented contract
build-artifacts.sh:79 — PACK_INVALID=1; STALE=1 — an invalid pack sets the same flag the doc says empties wiring.txt
build-artifacts.sh:368,400,441 — brief/label-probes/deps all correctly gate on [ "$STALE" = 0 ]
build-artifacts.sh:388 — if [ "$PACK_PRESENT" = 1 ]; then, with no STALE check, still populates wiring.txt from the flagged-invalid pack

findings.label: contract
findings.failure_mode: build-artifacts.sh fails/errors before printing OUT=, leaving OUT empty; grep against the resulting nonexistent "$OUT/wiring.txt" path exits non-zero (no-match), which the D1 check's else-branch reports as 'ok' instead of failing
evidence: tests/run-integration.sh:30 — OUT captured from build-artifacts.sh's stdout via grep '^OUT=', empty if the build errored out first
tests/run-integration.sh:32 — grep -qE '\$\(|echo' "$OUT/wiring.txt" 2>/dev/null becomes grep against "/wiring.txt", exits 2 (treated as no-match)
tests/run-integration.sh:36-37 — else branch prints 'ok D1: wiring.txt clean' even though the upstream build never produced anything to check

findings.label: duplication
findings.failure_mode: A domain pack missing/renaming one of the five required '## Heading' strings (e.g. '## Dependencies') is checked by two independently hand-written loops that disagree: build-artifacts.sh's own pre-existing inline loop (line 52) only warns to stderr and leaves STALE=0, so every other section still populates; the newly-wired call to validate-pack.sh (lines 76-83) re-implements the identical five-heading check and, on the same missing heading, exits 1, which build-artifacts.sh now treats as fatal (PACK_INVALID=1; STALE=1), blanking wiring.txt and every probes-*.txt that the first copy's warn-only path would have left intact.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:52 — `for h in "## Stack scope prefixes" ... "## Dependencies"; do grep -qxF "$h" "$PACK" || MISSING_HEADINGS=...` — inline heading check, warn-only, never sets STALE

.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:18 — `for h in "## Stack scope prefixes" ... "## Dependencies"; do grep -qxF "$h" "$PACK" || fail "missing or renamed heading: $h"` — a second, independently hand-written copy of the identical five-string check

.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:76-79 — new 0.1c wiring: `bash "$VALIDATOR" "$PACK"`; `if [ $? = 1 ]; then PACK_INVALID=1; STALE=1` — the second copy's failure now gates the whole pack

.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:368,400 — `if [ "$PACK_PRESENT" = 1 ] && [ "$STALE" = 0 ]` — STALE=1 from the duplicate check empties every probes file and wiring.txt for a miss the first copy alone would only have warned about
